summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of tracheobronchomalacia and tracheostomy status was admitted for persistent thick green secretions, dyspnea on exertion, and mild nausea. She had been evaluated in the ED previously and started on ciprofloxacin, but symptoms persisted, prompting admission for bronchoscopy. Imaging and labs showed no pneumonia or acute infection; sputum culture revealed only commensal flora. Bronchoscopy revealed supraglottic stenosis, leading to downsizing of her airway stent from size 7 to 6. Her symptoms improved with humidified air, albuterol nebulizers, montelukast, and Mucinex. Anemia with low ferritin was noted, and ferrous sulfate supplementation was initiated. She remained stable, tolerated the procedure well, and was discharged home with follow-up planned with interventional pulmonology and ENT. Her chronic conditions, including asthma, GERD, and depression, were managed with continued home medications.
